title: A table's rows as a price list: each name with its price on one line, a note under it, grouped under headings; or a rate table with labelled columns
about: Services and their prices, rates per hour or per page, plans, fees: the price never drifts away from its name, on a phone either. With COLUMNS it is a rate table (service, per hour, turnaround, best for) that becomes one card per row on a phone. Choose it whenever prices are listed; a table or cards are for comparing many other columns.

name.about: the column with each row's name

price.about: the column with its price (a number, or text such as 'from 40')

note.about: a column with a short line under the name

group.about: a column whose value is the heading a row goes under

badge.about: a column with a short word beside the name (New, Popular)

unit.about: words after every price (per hour, per page)

columns.about: a rate table instead of a list: [{key, label, format: money | number | text}], the first the name

where.about: an SQL condition on the rows

eyebrow.about: a short line above the heading

open.about: the view a row opens with {id} (to book or order it)

empty.about: words when there are no rows

data.{{key}}: SELECT * FROM {{table}}{{where|pre: WHERE }} ORDER BY {{order}} LIMIT 300

let.{{key}}_items: =({{key}} || []).map(r => Object.assign({}, r, {id: r.id, name: r[{{name|json}}], price: r[{{price|json}}], note: {{note|json}} ? r[{{note|json}}] : null, group: {{group|json}} ? r[{{group|json}}] : null, badge: {{badge|json}} ? r[{{badge|json}}] : null}))
